summary: At night, a black sedan with tinted windows glides past police cruisers to the hotel, and AGENT SMITH, AGENT BROWN, and AGENT JONES get out, all in dark suits and sunglasses, hardwired with Secret Service earphones. Agent Smith addresses the Lieutenant, who reacts with alarm ("Oh shit.") and then defiance, cursing the "Juris-my dick-tion" and rejecting the agents' authority. Agent Smith insists "The orders were for your protection," but the Lieutenant laughs, confident his units can handle "one little girl," and says he sent two units that are "bringing her down now." Agent Smith corrects him: "No, Lieutenant, your men are already dead," as he and Agent Brown start toward the hotel.

what_changes.before: Alarmed but trying to assert he is merely following procedure, saying "I'm just doing my job."
what_changes.after: Openly hostile and contemptuous toward the agents, cursing their orders and telling them to "cram it up your ass."
what_changes.evidence: You gimme that Juris-my dick-tion and you can cram it up your ass.

what_changes.before: The Lieutenant believes his men are still in control and "bringing her down now."
what_changes.after: Agent Smith reveals the men are already killed: "No, Lieutenant, your men are already dead."
what_changes.evidence: I sent two units.  They're bringing her down now.

event_hint.one_line: The agents arrive to take over the operation from the police, who believe they are capturing a fugitive girl.

minds.wants: To assert control of the operation and remove the police as an obstacle, treating the Lieutenant as a formality to be cleared rather than a negotiator.
minds.feels: A cold, patient contempt. He is not rattled by the Lieutenant's cursing because he already knows the outcome; the men are dead and the Lieutenant is, in Smith's mind, already obsolete.
minds.shows: Bureaucratic calm. He addresses the man by rank, frames the intervention as protection, and delivers the news of the deaths as a flat correction of a factual error — no triumph, no anger, just accuracy.
minds.basis: He greets the Lieutenant with 'Lieutenant?' and 'you were given specific orders,' then reframes the takeover as protection ('The orders were for your protection'), and closes by correcting the Lieutenant's assumption that his men are 'bringing her down now' with the flat statement that they are 'already dead.' His nod to Brown to proceed while still speaking shows he never needed the exchange to reach agreement.

believes_about.belief: That the Lieutenant is a jurisdictional nuisance to be managed with procedure-words, and that his defiance is irrelevant to the outcome.
believes_about.wrong_because: He underestimates that the Lieutenant's territorial pride is what will keep the police interfering and dying; the man is not simply an obstacle Smith can set aside but a variable that has already cost two units their lives and will continue to misread the threat.

believes_about.belief: That the Lieutenant still imagines his men are alive and in control.
believes_about.wrong_because: This is not wrong — it is exactly the delusion Smith exists to puncture, and Smith's final line is calibrated to that specific false belief.

minds.wants: To keep the Agents from taking over his operation — to defend his authority and his men's action against an outside power moving in on his case.
minds.feels: Alarm that instantly curdles into defensive rage. 'Oh shit' is genuine recognition of who these men are; the bluster that follows is a shield against being made small in front of his own officers.
minds.shows: Defiance and contempt — he mocks 'Juris-my dick-tion,' tells them to 'cram it up your ass,' and laughs, insisting 'we can handle one little girl.' He performs confidence he does not fully feel.
minds.basis: His arc is stated outright: he moves from alarmed ('Oh shit') and procedural ('I'm just doing my job') to openly hostile ('cram it up your ass'). He laughs while asserting they can handle 'one little girl,' and volunteers that he 'sent two units' that are 'bringing her down now' — a claim Smith then destroys.

believes_about.belief: That the Agents are paper-pushers trying to steal credit for a bust his unit is already finishing, and that their 'protection' framing is a lie covering a power grab.
believes_about.wrong_because: He reads them through the ordinary lens of inter-agency turf war. He cannot yet conceive that they are right about the danger — that his men are not 'bringing her down' but are already dead, meaning the Agents understand the target in a way he does not.

believes_about.belief: That she is 'one little girl' his units are 'bringing down now' — a trivial, contained fugitive.
believes_about.wrong_because: She has already killed the two units he believes are succeeding. His entire confident posture rests on a reality that no longer exists.

minds.wants: To move into the hotel and secure the target, following Smith's lead without needing to participate in the verbal standoff.
minds.feels: Nothing that requires expression here; he is the instrument, not the speaker, in this beat.
minds.shows: Silent readiness — he acts only on Smith's nod, stepping toward the hotel while Smith finishes the exchange. He lets Smith own the confrontation.
minds.basis: The only observable action is 'Agent Smith nods to Agent Brown as they start toward the hotel,' and the scene summary confirms 'he and Agent Brown start toward the hotel.' He says nothing and is given no reaction to read.

minds.wants: Nothing legible in this beat — he is present but given no action, line, or reaction.
minds.feels: Nothing the scene lets me read; assigning him an interior life here would be invention to fill the field.
minds.shows: Only that he exits the car with the others and stands with them. The scene does not use him.
minds.basis: The scene lists Jones among those who 'get out of the car' but gives him no dialogue, no described reaction, and no decision. Per the discipline that a character given no reaction has none legible, there is nothing to say.

connects_back: Depends on the police storming Room 303 and Trinity surrendering in sc-001 — the Agents arrive into an operation already in motion against a target they intend to take over.

The Lieutenant's belief that his men are 'bringing her down now' is the false premise the whole scene is built to demolish; it only has meaning because sc-001 established the squad already inside with Trinity.
The event shape (Agents arriving simultaneously to assert jurisdiction while the interior squad is already dead) is what licenses Smith's flat, untroubled certainty about the deaths.
sets_up: Makes possible the revelation that the interior police are dead and that Trinity is far more dangerous than 'one little girl,' which drives the rest of ev-001's rooftop chase.
Establishes the Agents' jurisdictional authority and their cold, procedural manner, which the later events (ev-003's office interrogation, ev-004's revelation) will redeploy against Neo.
Sets the Agents on their path into the hotel, which leads directly to their confirming no body remains and that Neo is the next target at the end of ev-001.
dramatic_function: To collide the ordinary law-enforcement world with the Agents' hidden, lethal authority — using the Lieutenant's territorial bluster as the foil against which Smith's inhuman calm and superior knowledge land, and delivering the dread twist (the men are already dead) that recontextualizes the entire raid.
